scope: Single-install PS5 A/B test under the normal ProsperoCraft title ID. Before JVM startup, choose the three-worker baseline or five-worker candidate with Left/Right and X. The JVM common pool is three for either choice. Uses the existing library and each instance’s saved render and simulation distance. Normal clean Quit Game performs the existing fresh-process restart, which presents the chooser again.
controls: The picker uses existing controller edge and neutral arming policy. A selection applies for the current process and is logged as PS5_CHUNK_TRIAL with the worker count and processor setting.
checks: 19 host policy and 13 native host checks passed.
Signed package and independent audit passed. The linked ELF contains both CPU configurations and log labels. 908 ZIP entries match the unpacked app.
console: The user compared Vanilla 26.3 and 1.21.11 on build 276. They report five workers felt faster and that chunk generation was fine after warmup. This is subjective feedback rather than a timed same-version comparison.

retrieved_evidence.retained_1_21_11: Five-worker run reached the integrated world. The game reported 1713 ms for the spawn preparation phase. ZGC logged roughly 70 ms concurrent allocation stalls across all five Worker-Main threads, the render thread and the server thread later in the run.
retrieved_evidence.current_26_3: Five-worker run reached the integrated world. The game reported 1032 ms for the spawn preparation phase. No allocation stall appears in the retrieved log.
retrieved_evidence.limits: Both retrieved game runs were configured for five workers. Different versions, warmup and uncontrolled workload preclude a three-versus-five speed calculation or a broad performance claim. Raw logs stay local.

disposition: Five workers are preferred for this test. No GC tuning was integrated after the warmup clarification.
